_doc: Topic bank for gen_plan.py --blog. Each build draws 3–5 unused topics. The model receives intent/angle/keywords and writes the article in the plan language; these entries are briefs, not the final copy. Keep ids stable: plans and profiles remember them to avoid repeating a topic in the same fleet.

topics.angle: Break down the true cost of using a platform: spreads, commissions, conversion, inactivity and withdrawal fees. Show a worked example and explain what to compare instead of the headline fee.
Explain the difference between an all-in spread and a separate commission, when each model costs more, and how to calculate the effective cost of a single position.
Give a practical procedure for checking a financial platform's registration: regulator register, legal entity name, licence number, country of operation and red flags.
Explain position risk in plain language: how much of an account a single position should risk, why stop levels matter, and how to keep a losing streak survivable.
Show how position size follows from account size, risk per position and distance to the stop. Include a simple formula and a worked example without promising outcomes.
Explain what volatility measures, why quiet and fast markets need different position sizes, and how volatility affects stops, spreads and slippage.
Compare market and limit orders by certainty of execution versus certainty of price. Explain when each is appropriate and how slippage appears in practice.
Describe the common ways a portfolio only looks diversified: correlated pairs, one theme in different wrappers, and concentration that appears after a big move.
Walk through the parts of a price quote: base and quote currency, bid, ask, spread, change and timestamp. Explain why two screens can show different numbers.
Explain liquidity in practical terms: why large orders move the price, when depth disappears, and how to reduce slippage around news and thin sessions.
Explain what a demo account can and cannot teach, which habits transfer to a live account, and how to move from practice to small real size without fooling yourself.
Outline the minimum viable trading plan: market, timeframe, entry and exit rules, risk cap, review cadence and what counts as a reason to stop for the day.
List the mistakes beginners repeat: oversized first trades, moving stops, averaging into a loser, changing strategy after two losses and skipping a written record.
Give a concrete account-security checklist: strong unique password, two-factor authentication, device review, withdrawal whitelist and how to react to a suspicious login.
Explain what to check before requesting a withdrawal: verification status, payment method rules, processing windows, fees and the fields that most often cause a delay.
Explain, in general terms, why trading records matter for tax reporting: statements, cost basis, holding periods and when to ask a local accountant instead of guessing.
Explain how to read an economic calendar: which releases move markets, what the forecast and previous columns mean, and why spreads widen around a release.
Explain leverage as borrowed exposure, not free money: how margin works, how quickly losses grow, and why lower leverage is a risk decision rather than a limitation.
Describe a lightweight trade journal: what to record, how to review a month of entries, and how to spot a pattern without turning the journal into a second job.
Explain how timeframe choice changes noise, holding time and the number of decisions per week. Help the reader match a timeframe to available time, not to ambition.
